input.command: ls -R | grep -v node_modules | head -50; cat -n src/routes.ts
cat -n src/worktree.ts src/store.ts src/config.ts; cat package.json; ls -a; grep -rn "validate\|registerRepo\|template\|buildRoutes" src

input.reason: No code checks repository ids anywhere in the repo. In src/routes.ts, registerRepo (lines 19-22) only checks that id is non-empty. It stores the id and calls cloneRepo, and cloneRepo in src/worktree.ts uses cachePath(id) = path.resolve(REPOS_DIR, id) as the clone destination. template (line 36) builds base = path.join(REPOS_DIR, req.params.id). Its startsWith(base) check on line 38 only keeps the file inside base, and the caller controls base, so a traversing id defeats the check. cacheListing (lines 60-61) reads path.resolve(REPOS_DIR, id)/INDEX. path.resolve with an absolute id like "/etc" ignores REPOS_DIR, and "../.." segments walk out of it. Store.insertRepo only runs a parameterized INSERT. config.ts sets REPOS_DIR to "/var/harbor/repos" and does no filtering. CLAUDE.md, which F14 cites, is not in the working tree. F14's claim does not depend on it, though: the template route really does use the raw id.
input.failure_scenario: A user posts registerRepo with body id "../../../tmp/evil". cloneRepo then runs git clone into /tmp/evil, outside /var/harbor/repos. On the template route, id "../../.." (for example, sent URL-encoded) makes base "/". A name of "../etc/passwd" then resolves to /etc/passwd, which passes the startsWith("/") check, and the file is returned. cacheListing with id "/etc" reads /etc/INDEX, and with id ".." it reads /var/harbor/INDEX.
input.severity_reason: The template route can read any file the process can read, and registerRepo can clone into any writable directory, so this is a real path traversal. How much of it can be exploited through URL params depends on how the router, which is not in the repo, decodes slashes. The body-supplied id in registerRepo is not limited by that. I rated it High rather than Critical because of that uncertainty.
